F-R48-1.correlation: NOT unique across runs: harness-core context.rs asset_local_test_context builds a fresh accord TransientCorrelation::new() (correlations 1, 2, ...) per call, i.e. per CLI invocation / viewer; a host context restarted the same way repeats its sequence. The new test pins it: two runs on one saved package with fresh sources mint the SAME correlation and command id for their develop commands.
F-R48-1.command_id: NOT unique: RUN_COMMANDS ids are static (e.g. layer.set_tiles_and_entry).
F-R48-1.client_session: NOT unique in the test host (fixed 'asset-local-test-host').
F-R48-1.event_sequence: per-run counter in Run (event_sequence), restarts at 0 per Run: the cause of the collision.
F-R48-1.choice: entry-only events (and the undo/redo of entry-only steps) keep revision = previous commit's (no revision semantics change, no golden changed) and take sequence = accord entry_event_sequence(event, token, before bytes, after bytes, command context) with the top bit set (ENTRY_EVENT_SEQUENCE_BIT): commit events keep 0, 1, ... so the two id spaces never meet; two runs that change an entry differently mint different ids; two records with one id carry the same envelope context (a replay, never a counted collision) unless the 63-bit FNV-1a+SplitMix64 hash collides (disclosed). kernel-bindings' envelope check event_id == business_event_id(document, revision, sequence) is unchanged and holds.
F-R48-1.rejected: entry writes advancing a revision (changes what a revision means; other lanes' goldens observe revisions); correlation-only ids (not unique across runs, measured); persisting the sequence with the document (a hidden entry would change saved package bytes)

F-R48-3.measured_at: recorded 2026-10-31T13:37:08Z (static reading of the base 4f69b03b done before the fix was chosen)
F-R48-3.correlation_source: the viewer's Run holds the RunContext (Viewer::with_context / Viewer::new); RunContext::command mints from its shared correlation source, so JobAdmission binds a RunCorrelations adapter over a clone of it (clones share the source).
